sg-9Mue.title: Sign: green direction sign, 3-letter expressway
sg-9Mue.summary: Direction signs are green with white English text. Each expressway has a three-letter code, such as TPE, which makes them easy to spot.

sg-KPH6.title: Area: resort island, green signs, winding roads
sg-KPH6.summary: A resort island with green signposts, winding roads and a holiday feel. You may spot a green lane marking too.

sg-LCE7.title: Paths: red paving stones everywhere
sg-LCE7.summary: A tiny island where the whole walkway is paved with red stones.

sg-NOTm.title: Vehicles: lime-green buses
sg-NOTm.summary: Buses are mostly lime green. Other colours exist too, like the white-and-purple SBS Transit buses.

sg-RNhX.title: Bollard: concrete with black-yellow bands
sg-RNhX.summary: Bus stops are protected by concrete bollards with black-and-yellow warning bands. Some Malaysian cities have similar, but not identical, ones.

differs.how: Similar bollards in some cities, but the design is not identical

sg-SP7M.title: Google car: Gen 3 walker, forest and camo hat
sg-SP7M.summary: A Gen 3 backpack camera on a rural, forested island. Looking down, you may see the walker's camouflage-style hat.

sg-TWrN.title: Google car: Gen 3 walker, smooth roads, sea
sg-TWrN.summary: Two small islands filmed on foot with the Gen 3 camera. Smooth asphalt roads, and the sea is almost always close.

sg-U9vA.title: Plants: rain trees along main roads
sg-U9vA.summary: Rain trees, wide trees with big spreading crowns, are common and often planted along main roads.

sg-dONA.title: Vibe: clean city-state, tall apartment blocks
sg-dONA.summary: A very clean, orderly city. Divided main roads, black-and-white curbs, double yellow lines at the edge, and tall apartment blocks nearby. Often enough on its own.

sg-gJnM.title: Sign: road signs on a white square
sg-gJnM.summary: Road signs sit on a square white background. Almost no other country does this.

sg-hHxa.title: Traffic lights: curved metal sheet with holes
sg-hHxa.summary: Almost all traffic lights are backed by a curved sheet of metal with several holes in it.

sg-hevr.title: Road markings: big warning words, HUMP AHEAD
sg-hevr.summary: Warnings are painted on the road in large letters, such as the well-known HUMP AHEAD.

sg-lm-12982.title: Sign: stop sign with white square outline
sg-lm-12982.summary: Stop signs have a white square outline around the red shape, which makes them unique.

sg-mfCc.title: Plate: black with white text, not split
sg-mfCc.summary: Most plates are black with white text. Older ones can be white-and-yellow, and red is very rare. Malaysia and Indonesia look alike, but their letters are split into sections.

differs.how: Letters are split into two or three sections
Letters are split into two or three sections

sg-nZF6.title: Landscape: industrial area, cranes, containers
sg-nZF6.summary: A western industrial zone with straight roads, big factories, cranes and shipping containers.

sg-oACN.title: Sign: green street name, rounded corners
sg-oACN.summary: Street name signs are green with rounded corners and a distinctive white font. This format is unique to the country.

sg-sB3c.title: Sign: street named after the neighbourhood
sg-sB3c.summary: Suburban streets are often named after their neighbourhood, e.g. Street 31 in Ang Mo Kio. That lets you find the area on the map quickly.

sg-su01.title: Road markings: yellow bus-leaving box with arrow
sg-su01.summary: Besides the bollards, bus stops sometimes have a yellow box painted on the road with an arrow, where buses pull out.
